References: @image1 is the look of the onboard close-up through Theo's visor; @image2 is the look of Dana Reyes at the PushOwl Racing pit wall; @image3 is the look of the over-the-shoulder cockpit view; @image4 is the look of the PushOwl Racing car passing the sponsor boards; @image5 is the look of the side mirror with the orange Ember Racing car closing; @image6 is the look of the two cars wheel to wheel; @image7 is the look of the PushOwl Racing pit box; @image8 is Theo Vance's face; @image9 is Dana Reyes's face; @image10 is PushOwl Racing livery, suit and helmet board; @image11 is trackside barrier, grandstand and gantry board; @image12 is PushOwl Racing garage and pit board; @image13 is Ember Racing (orange rival) logo. @audio1 is ONLY the voice of Dana Reyes, @audio2 is ONLY the voice of Theo Vance: match their timbre, pitch and accent exactly and keep each voice identical in every line; the words in the voice samples are not part of this film and are never spoken.
A 30 second cinematic race thriller, one continuous generation of ten shots, the Port Aurelia Night Race. Vertical 9:16, ultra-real, ARRI Alexa 35 look, Kodak 500T grain, rich night blacks, cool floodlight and warm sodium at the track. Hard motivated cuts, fast camera. Faces, wardrobe, the green PushOwl Racing car no. 7 and every logo exactly as in the references. BRANDS: the only logos anywhere are the fictional ones on the supplied brand boards (Meridian Series, Port Aurelia Night Race, PushOwl Racing, KALOR, GRAVIK, HALDEN, VOLTIQ, ZENTEL, HAULIX, Ember Racing, Altair Racing, Burnt Rubber Candle Co.); every other sign or screen is blank. Phone and laptop screens always face away from camera. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles.
FRAMING: from 6.5 s to 28.5 s every shot keeps its subject and all action inside the middle half of the frame height (the picture will be cropped to a wide band), nothing important in the top or bottom quarter.
SOUND: NO MUSIC AT ALL, no score, no drums, no stings (music is added later). The soundtrack is only the spoken lines plus natural sound: engines, tyres, crowd, radio texture, room tone. Engines scream, sparks crackle, the crowd roars; there are deliberate one-second beats of pure engine sound between some lines, as marked.
VOICES: Dana, @audio1. Theo, @audio2. TV commentator: American male, big broadcast baritone, fast and excited, heard as a live broadcast feed. Spotter: American male, clipped tenor on the team radio, calm and precise, clearly different from Theo.
PHYSICS: every object keeps one consistent physical state within a shot; phones and helmets never flip, morph or change shape; no flashes or glitch frames.
0 to 1.6 s: extreme close-up onboard through Theo's visor at 300 km/h, sparks streaking. The TV commentator, excited and fast: "Lap forty-one, and Vance is hunting Castell!"
1.6 to 4.8 s: Dana Reyes on camera at the PushOwl Racing pit wall, headset mic at her lips, she turns to the lens-side monitor and speaks, urgent but deadpan, stress on "Brenda": "Theo. Your store. Brenda just abandoned her cart."
4.8 to 6.5 s: over-the-shoulder cockpit view, circuit rushing at camera. Theo on the radio, cool and almost amused: "Relax. It's on autopilot."
6.5 to 9.5 s: camera rides low alongside the PushOwl Racing car past the sponsor boards. Dana on the radio, clipped: "Push sent." Then one second of pure engine roar. Then Dana, flat and dry: "Dismissed."
9.5 to 13 s: extreme close-up of the side mirror, the orange Ember Racing car growing closer. The spotter, clipped and calm: "Castell behind. Half a second." Dana on the radio, quick: "Email's out."
13 to 17 s: tight on Theo's eyes through the visor, jaw set. The TV commentator, rising: "Castell is all over the back of him!" One second of engine roar. Dana on the radio, same voice, slightly faster: "Email unopened."
17 to 21 s: cockpit view, sparks off the floor. Theo on the radio, low, firm and calm: "Text her." Dana on the radio, focused: "SMS going out." Then one and a half seconds of pure engine roar.
21 to 25 s: the orange Ember Racing car lunges alongside, wheel to wheel through a fast corner. The spotter, urgent and rising: "Side by side. Hold it. Hold it!" The TV commentator, relieved: "Vance just about keeps it!"
25 to 28.5 s: Dana on camera at the pit wall, decisive, eyes on her screen: "Box, box, Theo. One last shot." The car peels into the pit lane; Theo on the radio, one calm word: "Copy."
28.5 to 30 s: the PushOwl Racing car slides into its pit box, the crew braced, a heartbeat of stillness.
DELIVERY: every quoted line is spoken clearly, exactly as written, once, acted not read, the noted emotion in the face (on camera) and voice, natural breaths, stressed words stressed. Radio lines are clear and lightly compressed, never muffled. Nothing outside the quotes is ever spoken.
